notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after five searches (the first two candidates). Everything else was read by opening pages directly, with the kit's honest User-Agent and each site's robots.txt obeyed, or with the page-reading tool: the candidates' own sites, each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's list of endorsed candidates and local party units' pages, the University of Minnesota's election archive, Wikipedia, and a few local news sites' own pages (CCX Media, KYMN Radio, the Enterprise Dispatch, Southwest News Media, WJON). No search engine was read in place of the search tool.

The campaign websites the candidates filed were learned from a scratch copy of the database on which the kit's own step (python -m ballot.local_sites files) had been run; each was then opened. Four more were found: Thaddeus Laugisch's (the Clay County DFL's page gives it), Peder Jothen's (KYMN Radio's candidate guide gives it), and Jeremiah Sedler's and Gerry Hoisington's (reached by trying an address; each was kept only because its own pages name the office, the place and this year's election). Other addresses that answered were not campaign sites for these races and were dropped.

Three campaign sites answered the kit's script with 429 (too many requests) on some or all requests and were read with the page-reading tool: danrogersmn.com, ronnenbergformn.com (its robots.txt could not be read either) and clarkforplymouth.com (which leads to www.clarkgregor.com; the Meet Clark page there did answer the script). The second reader may meet the same 429.

Clark Gregor: the address he filed, clarkforplymouth.com, redirects to www.clarkgregor.com. The filed address is given as the website so the loader sees it as the filed one; his campaign-sourced offices cite pages on www.clarkgregor.com. The Senate District 43 DFL's page lists him under "Letters of Support", which the DFL gives in nonpartisan races instead of an endorsement; it is recorded under endorsed_by with that wording kept in the unit text, for the second reader to judge. His campaign site lists his council seat as 2023 to present; the city's page gives only the end of the term, so the official entry has no start year.
Peder Jothen's own site says the DFL gave him a letter of support; no DFL page naming him was found (the Rice/Scott 58 DFL's candidates page does not), so it is recorded as his own words only.

Brad Olson: the election archive's page is for a Brad Olson of Brooklyn Park who was the Republican candidate in House District 38A in 2024. No page read states in so many words that he is this year's Senate District 38 candidate; the tie is the name, the party and the place (38A is half of Senate District 38), and CCX Media covered both runs. Left for the second reader to judge. His campaign site showed only its title.

The Minnesota Historical Election Archive (University of Minnesota Libraries) is the source for three earlier runs under a party label (Brad Olson, Thaddeus Laugisch, Jen Fox, all 2024). It is a university archive of official returns, not a news organization, and is labelled secondary for the second reader to judge. The birth dates it shows for the three were not taken, because the source it names for them is a birth records index.
No birth year is recorded for anyone. Wikipedia's article on Sarah Hennesy gives "born 1969 or 1970", which is not a year; Allen Miskowiec's site gives an age without a date.

Not read, and nothing worked around: the Minnesota Judicial Branch's site (403 to the script's robots.txt request and to the page-reading tool), so Sarah Hennesy has no official page here and nothing is recorded for Judge Andrew Pearson; Becker County's site (a certificate chain the kit's check would not accept at one address, a Radware page at the other); mshale.com and the Freeborn County Republicans' site (403 and no answer). The Governor's office release of April 22, 2024 announcing Sarah Hennesy's appointment (https://mn.gov/governor/newsroom/press-releases/?id=1055-621124) was read once; a second request to mn.gov met a Radware CAPTCHA and the host was left alone, so her offices rest on her campaign site.

The Detroit Lakes Tribune's robots.txt asks Claude by name to stay out. Two of its pages (the Election 2026 index and a story on the Becker County auditor-treasurer forum) were opened with the kit's script before that was noticed; nothing is cited from them, and the story named no public office or campaign website for Amy Rosing.
Republican endorsements: none could be recorded for Brad Olson or Nick Ronnenberg. mngop.com lists statewide nominees only, and no local unit's page naming either was found.

Patrick Barry's site lists "Planning Commission" and "Charter Commission" under civic leadership without naming the city or the years, so no office is recorded from it; his posts in the sheriff's office are employment, not offices. Gary Gray's county page also names a fire board, a library board and two industry boards; only the township board and the federal appointment are recorded.

Nothing citable was found for eight candidates, who are listed with no findings: Daniel Widmer, Jim Muelken, Amy Rosing, Tony Khambata, Chet Gunhus, Rick Deinken, Dario Garcia and Andrew Pearson. The official pages read show that six of them do not hold the office sought today: Sibley County lists Peter Koch for District 1 and Scott County lists Tom Wolf for District 2, and the Cottage Grove council page and the Eastern Carver County, Dassel-Cokato and Faribault school board pages do not list Tony Khambata, Chet Gunhus, Rick Deinken or Dario Garcia. Jeremiah Sedler is likewise not on the Cambridge council page.

Second reading, 2026-10-02: every address was re-opened with the kit's script (robots.txt read first for each host) and the wording compared. danrogersmn.com, clarkforplymouth.com and www.clarkgregor.com answered the script with 429 twice and were read with the page-reading tool, which confirmed them; www.ronnenbergformn.com could not be read either way, so both of Nick Ronnenberg's findings were deleted (his filed address is still in the Secretary of State's list). Clark Gregor's letter of support was taken out of endorsed_by because the unit's own page sets letters of support apart from endorsements. Kept for the reasons the first reader gave, and worth John's eye: Brad Olson's 2024 run (the archive does not mention 2026; name, state, party and place agree) and Samba Fall's website (it names him and the Maple Grove City Council, but every dated item on it is from 2024). The election archive is kept as secondary. 67 findings confirmed, 3 deleted.
